steps.caption: Draw four boxes: a bar across the top, two side by side, a strip along the bottom. Each reads as a rectangle, with the measurement that says so.
Take the offer to draw them clean. The ink stays underneath; the clean forms are what the page will be built inside.
Circle the four. The loop is held: a lasso until the next mark says otherwise, a circle if you draw on.
Cross it with the command mark. The palette reads the drawing: boxes tiling a space — a layout — and offers what it could become.
Say "a page". The engine hands the model the layout it measured and the drawing as the brief — what each box plays, how they sit — and asks only for the content. The page renders inside your ink.
Draw on the page itself. A loop over the running page is a lasso even though it encloses no mark: it encloses a region, and the engine says which one. The offer is now a change, not a build.
Say what should change. Only the region the ink addressed is rewritten; the rest of the page is exactly as it was, and both versions are held.
